theory.levelNote: Basic order is subject + verb + object. Questions often use be / do at the front.
points: I / you / she / he + am / is / are.
A / an with a singular count noun: a café, an apple.
Present simple for habits: I work, she works.
There is / there are for what exists.
Can for ability or a polite request: Can I have tea?
Yes–no questions: put be / do / can first.
Possessive: my / your / her + noun, or noun + 's.
There is / there are for existence.
This / that / these / those for near and far.
Number + noun: two teas, three friends. Use a for one countable.
Present simple: I go, she goes. Add -s for he / she / it.
Please at the start or end makes a request polite.
Don't + verb for a negative in the present.
contrasts: I am Lan / My name is Lan — both work; the second highlights the name.
Don't eat = refusal. I haven't eaten = not yet.
A café / an apple — a before a consonant sound, an before a vowel sound.
What asks for a thing, where for a place, yes–no with be / do.
mistakes: Dropping be: *I Lan. Fix: I am Lan.
Wrong article: *a apple. Fix: an apple.
No -s: *She work. Fix: She works.
Word-for-word translation that breaks English order.
examples: I am Lan. I am not hungry.
Where are you? I am at home.
It is seven in the morning.
Sorry, I do not understand yet.

goal.en: Order food, say taste, ask for more.

goal.th: สั่งอาหาร บอกรส ขอเพิ่ม

theory.levelNote: Add time: past simple, going to, and comparatives. Countable vs uncountable starts to matter.
points: Past simple: I went, she had, we did.
Going to for a near plan.
Comparative: cheaper, nearer, more expensive.
Some / any in offers and questions.
Could I…? is softer than Can I…?
Present continuous: am / is / are + -ing for now.
Past simple for a finished time: yesterday, last week.
Going to + verb for a near plan.
Comparative: adjective + -er, or more + adjective.
Could you…? / Can I…? for polite requests.
Why? to ask for a short reason.
Before / after + time or clause.
Too / enough: too spicy, not big enough.
contrasts: I am eating (now) vs I ate (finished) vs I am going to eat (plan).
Cheaper compares two. The cheapest is for more than two.
Could I…? is softer than Can I…?
A bit / quite change strength, not yes–no.
mistakes: Present simple with yesterday: *I go yesterday. Fix: I went.
Forgetting irregular past: go→went, have→had, eat→ate.
Comparative without than when you name both things.
Using will for a near personal plan when going to is clearer.
examples: I am eating. I have already eaten.
Tomorrow I am going to go. Yesterday I went.
I do not understand it all yet.
What would you like to drink?

theory.tip: Regular past adds -ed; many daily verbs are irregular.
theory.structure: Taste comes after the dish: not spicy, a bit sweet. State allergies clearly.

patterns.note: Not with a finished time.
Many daily verbs are irregular.

patterns.example: I am going to the market tomorrow.
patterns.note: Clearer than will for a personal plan.
Add than that if you name both.
Softer than Can you.

patterns.form: I have not + past participle + yet.
patterns.note: Yet = still waiting.

theory.levelNote: Basic order is subject + verb + object. Questions often use be / do at the front.
points: I / you / she / he + am / is / are.
A / an with a singular count noun: a café, an apple.
Present simple for habits: I work, she works.
There is / there are for what exists.
Can for ability or a polite request: Can I have tea?
Yes–no questions: put be / do / can first.
Possessive: my / your / her + noun, or noun + 's.
There is / there are for existence.
This / that / these / those for near and far.
Number + noun: two teas, three friends. Use a for one countable.
Present simple: I go, she goes. Add -s for he / she / it.
Please at the start or end makes a request polite.
Don't + verb for a negative in the present.
contrasts: I am Lan / My name is Lan — both work; the second highlights the name.
Don't eat = refusal. I haven't eaten = not yet.
A café / an apple — a before a consonant sound, an before a vowel sound.
What asks for a thing, where for a place, yes–no with be / do.
mistakes: Dropping be: *I Lan. Fix: I am Lan.
Wrong article: *a apple. Fix: an apple.
No -s: *She work. Fix: She works.
Word-for-word translation that breaks English order.

Where are you? I am at home.
It is seven in the morning.
Sorry, I do not understand yet.

I'd like to try a larger size.

theory.levelNote: Basic order is subject + verb + object. Questions often use be / do at the front.
points: I / you / she / he + am / is / are.
A / an with a singular count noun: a café, an apple.
Present simple for habits: I work, she works.
There is / there are for what exists.
Can for ability or a polite request: Can I have tea?
Yes–no questions: put be / do / can first.
Possessive: my / your / her + noun, or noun + 's.
There is / there are for existence.
This / that / these / those for near and far.
Number + noun: two teas, three friends. Use a for one countable.
Present simple: I go, she goes. Add -s for he / she / it.
Please at the start or end makes a request polite.
Don't + verb for a negative in the present.
contrasts: I am Lan / My name is Lan — both work; the second highlights the name.
Don't eat = refusal. I haven't eaten = not yet.
A café / an apple — a before a consonant sound, an before a vowel sound.
What asks for a thing, where for a place, yes–no with be / do.
mistakes: Dropping be: *I Lan. Fix: I am Lan.
Wrong article: *a apple. Fix: an apple.
No -s: *She work. Fix: She works.
Word-for-word translation that breaks English order.
examples: I am Lan. I am not hungry.
Where are you? I am at home.
It is seven in the morning.
Sorry, I do not understand yet.
The shirt is old but still fine.

theory.levelNote: Link ideas: because, if, so, when. Present perfect vs past. Soft opinion with I think / I need.
points: Present perfect: I have arrived, I have forgotten.
First conditional: If it rains, I will stay.
Should / might for advice and possibility.
Because / so / although for reason and contrast.
I would like… for a polite want.
If + present, will + verb for a real future condition.
Because / so link a reason and a result.
To + verb for a purpose.
When / after / before to order events.
Present perfect for a result that matters now.
I think / I feel for a soft opinion.
Although… , … for a simple concession.
Need to / have to / should — different strength.
contrasts: If… will… = a real condition. Because / so = reason and result.
I have arrived (result now) vs I arrived yesterday (finished time).
Should = advice. Might = possibility.
I think is softer than I am sure.
mistakes: If + will: *If it will rain…. Fix: If it rains, I will…
Present perfect with a finished date: *I have gone yesterday.
Advice as an order: Use should, not must, in daily talk.
Opinion with no reason — add because.
examples: If it rains, I will stay home.
I came early so I would not be late.
I am late because of the traffic.
I think we should call back.
I will transfer it to you.
This fee is a bit high.

theory.levelNote: Link ideas: because, if, so, when. Present perfect vs past. Soft opinion with I think / I need.
points: Present perfect: I have arrived, I have forgotten.
First conditional: If it rains, I will stay.
Should / might for advice and possibility.
Because / so / although for reason and contrast.
I would like… for a polite want.
If + present, will + verb for a real future condition.
Because / so link a reason and a result.
To + verb for a purpose.
When / after / before to order events.
Present perfect for a result that matters now.
I think / I feel for a soft opinion.
Although… , … for a simple concession.
Need to / have to / should — different strength.
contrasts: If… will… = a real condition. Because / so = reason and result.
I have arrived (result now) vs I arrived yesterday (finished time).
Should = advice. Might = possibility.
I think is softer than I am sure.
mistakes: If + will: *If it will rain…. Fix: If it rains, I will…
Present perfect with a finished date: *I have gone yesterday.
Advice as an order: Use should, not must, in daily talk.
Opinion with no reason — add because.
examples: If it rains, I will stay home.
I came early so I would not be late.
I am late because of the traffic.
I think we should call back.
I will transfer it to you.
This fee is a bit high.

Need to / have to / should — different strength.

theory.levelNote: Link ideas: because, if, so, when. Present perfect vs past. Soft opinion with I think / I need.
points: Present perfect: I have arrived, I have forgotten.
First conditional: If it rains, I will stay.
Should / might for advice and possibility.
Because / so / although for reason and contrast.
I would like… for a polite want.
If + present, will + verb for a real future condition.
Because / so link a reason and a result.
To + verb for a purpose.
When / after / before to order events.
Present perfect for a result that matters now.
I think / I feel for a soft opinion.
Although… , … for a simple concession.
Need to / have to / should — different strength.
contrasts: If… will… = a real condition. Because / so = reason and result.
I have arrived (result now) vs I arrived yesterday (finished time).
Should = advice. Might = possibility.
I think is softer than I am sure.
mistakes: If + will: *If it will rain…. Fix: If it rains, I will…
Present perfect with a finished date: *I have gone yesterday.
Advice as an order: Use should, not must, in daily talk.
Opinion with no reason — add because.

I came early so I would not be late.
I am late because of the traffic.
I think we should call back.

theory.levelNote: Link ideas: because, if, so, when. Present perfect vs past. Soft opinion with I think / I need.
points: Present perfect: I have arrived, I have forgotten.
First conditional: If it rains, I will stay.
Should / might for advice and possibility.
Because / so / although for reason and contrast.
I would like… for a polite want.
If + present, will + verb for a real future condition.
Because / so link a reason and a result.
To + verb for a purpose.
When / after / before to order events.
Present perfect for a result that matters now.
I think / I feel for a soft opinion.
Although… , … for a simple concession.
Need to / have to / should — different strength.
contrasts: If… will… = a real condition. Because / so = reason and result.
I have arrived (result now) vs I arrived yesterday (finished time).
Should = advice. Might = possibility.
I think is softer than I am sure.
mistakes: If + will: *If it will rain…. Fix: If it rains, I will…
Present perfect with a finished date: *I have gone yesterday.
Advice as an order: Use should, not must, in daily talk.
Opinion with no reason — add because.
examples: If it rains, I will stay home.
I came early so I would not be late.
I am late because of the traffic.
I think we should call back.

theory.tip: If + present, will + verb.
theory.structure: Internet: wifi, password, slow, send a file, join a call.

theory.levelNote: Basic order is subject + verb + object. Questions often use be / do at the front.
points: I / you / she / he + am / is / are.
A / an with a singular count noun: a café, an apple.
Present simple for habits: I work, she works.
There is / there are for what exists.
Can for ability or a polite request: Can I have tea?
Yes–no questions: put be / do / can first.
Possessive: my / your / her + noun, or noun + 's.
There is / there are for existence.
This / that / these / those for near and far.
Number + noun: two teas, three friends. Use a for one countable.
Present simple: I go, she goes. Add -s for he / she / it.
Please at the start or end makes a request polite.
Don't + verb for a negative in the present.
contrasts: I am Lan / My name is Lan — both work; the second highlights the name.
Don't eat = refusal. I haven't eaten = not yet.
A café / an apple — a before a consonant sound, an before a vowel sound.
What asks for a thing, where for a place, yes–no with be / do.
mistakes: Dropping be: *I Lan. Fix: I am Lan.
Wrong article: *a apple. Fix: an apple.
No -s: *She work. Fix: She works.
Word-for-word translation that breaks English order.
examples: I am Lan. I am not hungry.
Where are you? I am at home.
It is seven in the morning.
Sorry, I do not understand yet.
The one in the blue shirt is him.
It does not look like the photo.

points: Present perfect: I have arrived, I have forgotten.
First conditional: If it rains, I will stay.
Should / might for advice and possibility.
Because / so / although for reason and contrast.
I would like… for a polite want.
If + present, will + verb for a real future condition.
Because / so link a reason and a result.
To + verb for a purpose.
When / after / before to order events.
Present perfect for a result that matters now.

Although… , … for a simple concession.

contrasts: If… will… = a real condition. Because / so = reason and result.

theory.levelNote: Add time: past simple, going to, and comparatives. Countable vs uncountable starts to matter.
points: Past simple: I went, she had, we did.
Going to for a near plan.
Comparative: cheaper, nearer, more expensive.
Some / any in offers and questions.
Could I…? is softer than Can I…?
Present continuous: am / is / are + -ing for now.
Past simple for a finished time: yesterday, last week.
Going to + verb for a near plan.
Comparative: adjective + -er, or more + adjective.
Could you…? / Can I…? for polite requests.
Why? to ask for a short reason.
Before / after + time or clause.
Too / enough: too spicy, not big enough.
contrasts: I am eating (now) vs I ate (finished) vs I am going to eat (plan).
Cheaper compares two. The cheapest is for more than two.
Could I…? is softer than Can I…?
A bit / quite change strength, not yes–no.
mistakes: Present simple with yesterday: *I go yesterday. Fix: I went.
Forgetting irregular past: go→went, have→had, eat→ate.
Comparative without than when you name both things.
Using will for a near personal plan when going to is clearer.
examples: I am eating. I have already eaten.
Tomorrow I am going to go. Yesterday I went.
I do not understand it all yet.

Are there tickets for the nine o'clock showing?

points: Past simple: I went, she had, we did.

Why? to ask for a short reason.
Before / after + time or clause.

contrasts: I am eating (now) vs I ate (finished) vs I am going to eat (plan).

Could I…? is softer than Can I…?

theory.levelNote: Link ideas: because, if, so, when. Present perfect vs past. Soft opinion with I think / I need.
points: Present perfect: I have arrived, I have forgotten.
First conditional: If it rains, I will stay.
Should / might for advice and possibility.
Because / so / although for reason and contrast.
I would like… for a polite want.
If + present, will + verb for a real future condition.
Because / so link a reason and a result.
To + verb for a purpose.
When / after / before to order events.
Present perfect for a result that matters now.
I think / I feel for a soft opinion.
Although… , … for a simple concession.
Need to / have to / should — different strength.
contrasts: If… will… = a real condition. Because / so = reason and result.
I have arrived (result now) vs I arrived yesterday (finished time).
Should = advice. Might = possibility.
I think is softer than I am sure.
mistakes: If + will: *If it will rain…. Fix: If it rains, I will…

examples: If it rains, I will stay home.
I came early so I would not be late.
I am late because of the traffic.

theory.levelNote: Link ideas: because, if, so, when. Present perfect vs past. Soft opinion with I think / I need.
points: Present perfect: I have arrived, I have forgotten.
First conditional: If it rains, I will stay.
Should / might for advice and possibility.
Because / so / although for reason and contrast.
I would like… for a polite want.
If + present, will + verb for a real future condition.
Because / so link a reason and a result.
To + verb for a purpose.
When / after / before to order events.
Present perfect for a result that matters now.
I think / I feel for a soft opinion.
Although… , … for a simple concession.
Need to / have to / should — different strength.
contrasts: If… will… = a real condition. Because / so = reason and result.
I have arrived (result now) vs I arrived yesterday (finished time).

mistakes: If + will: *If it will rain…. Fix: If it rains, I will…

Opinion with no reason — add because.
examples: If it rains, I will stay home.

title.th: การร้องเรียนอย่างสุภาพ · ทฤษฎี

goal.vi: Nói sự cố, xin đổi, giữ giọng lịch sự.
goal.en: Name the problem, ask for a change, stay polite.
goal.zh: 说明问题、请求更换，并保持礼貌。
goal.th: บอกปัญหา ขอเปลี่ยน และรักษาน้ำเสียงสุภาพ

theory.levelNote: Control stance: although, however, if I were, on the other hand. Soften disagreement.
points: Although / however for contrast.
Second conditional: If I were you, I would…
Passive when the action matters more than the person.
I see your point, but…
Tend to / might to avoid sounding absolute.
Although / even if… still… to concede, then keep your stance.
If I were / if I had for hypotheticals.
On the one hand… on the other… to show two sides.
Not really / not necessarily / perhaps to avoid sounding absolute.
I see your point, but… to disagree politely.
Instead of… I would… to offer another way.
It is not that… it is that… to reframe.
Spoken tone: skip furthermore / thus in a café talk.
contrasts: Although / still = concession. But is sharper.
If I were you = hypothetical, not a real plan.
Not really / not necessarily softens a claim.
I see your point, but… disagrees without a fight.
mistakes: Long sentences with no stance.
Disagreeing without an alternative.
Essay connectors (furthermore, thus) in a café conversation.
Using always / definitely with no evidence.
examples: Although I am tired, I still study for 15 minutes.
If I were late, I would send a message.
I understand you are busy, but I need this changed.
On the one hand it is convenient; on the other it is noisy.
This may not work for everyone.
Sorry, this dish is not right.
I have waited quite a long time.
Could you replace this for me?
I am a bit disappointed this time.
I would like to see the manager.
I hope next time it will be quicker.
If possible, I would like a partial refund.
I am still keeping a polite tone.
theory.applyPrompt: Give an opinion plus a contrast or condition.
theory.tip: B2 is tone control, not longer sentences for their own sake.
theory.structure: Sorry + the problem + ask to replace / refund. Stay polite.

theory.levelNote: Control stance: although, however, if I were, on the other hand. Soften disagreement.
points: Although / however for contrast.
Second conditional: If I were you, I would…
Passive when the action matters more than the person.
I see your point, but…
Tend to / might to avoid sounding absolute.
Although / even if… still… to concede, then keep your stance.
If I were / if I had for hypotheticals.
On the one hand… on the other… to show two sides.
Not really / not necessarily / perhaps to avoid sounding absolute.
I see your point, but… to disagree politely.
Instead of… I would… to offer another way.
It is not that… it is that… to reframe.
Spoken tone: skip furthermore / thus in a café talk.
contrasts: Although / still = concession. But is sharper.
If I were you = hypothetical, not a real plan.
Not really / not necessarily softens a claim.
I see your point, but… disagrees without a fight.
mistakes: Long sentences with no stance.
Disagreeing without an alternative.
Essay connectors (furthermore, thus) in a café conversation.
Using always / definitely with no evidence.
examples: Although I am tired, I still study for 15 minutes.
If I were late, I would send a message.
I understand you are busy, but I need this changed.
On the one hand it is convenient; on the other it is noisy.
This may not work for everyone.
Sorry, this dish is not right.
I have waited quite a long time.
Could you replace this for me?
I am a bit disappointed this time.
theory.applyPrompt: Give an opinion plus a contrast or condition.
theory.tip: B2 is tone control, not longer sentences for their own sake.
theory.structure: Sorry + the problem + ask to replace / refund. Stay polite.

theory.levelNote: Control stance: although, however, if I were, on the other hand. Soften disagreement.
points: Although / however for contrast.
Second conditional: If I were you, I would…
Passive when the action matters more than the person.
I see your point, but…
Tend to / might to avoid sounding absolute.
Although / even if… still… to concede, then keep your stance.
If I were / if I had for hypotheticals.
On the one hand… on the other… to show two sides.
Not really / not necessarily / perhaps to avoid sounding absolute.
I see your point, but… to disagree politely.
Instead of… I would… to offer another way.
It is not that… it is that… to reframe.
Spoken tone: skip furthermore / thus in a café talk.
contrasts: Although / still = concession. But is sharper.
If I were you = hypothetical, not a real plan.
Not really / not necessarily softens a claim.
I see your point, but… disagrees without a fight.
mistakes: Long sentences with no stance.
Disagreeing without an alternative.
Essay connectors (furthermore, thus) in a café conversation.
Using always / definitely with no evidence.
examples: Although I am tired, I still study for 15 minutes.
If I were late, I would send a message.
I understand you are busy, but I need this changed.
On the one hand it is convenient; on the other it is noisy.
This may not work for everyone.
If possible, I would like a partial refund.
I am still keeping a polite tone.
theory.applyPrompt: Give an opinion plus a contrast or condition.
theory.tip: B2 is tone control, not longer sentences for their own sake.
theory.structure: Sorry + the problem + ask to replace / refund. Stay polite.

points: Although / however for contrast.
Second conditional: If I were you, I would…

Not really / not necessarily / perhaps to avoid sounding absolute.

Instead of… I would… to offer another way.
It is not that… it is that… to reframe.

contrasts: Although / still = concession. But is sharper.
If I were you = hypothetical, not a real plan.
Not really / not necessarily softens a claim.

mistakes: Long sentences with no stance.

I hope next time it will be quicker.

theory.levelNote: Control stance: although, however, if I were, on the other hand. Soften disagreement.
points: Although / however for contrast.
Second conditional: If I were you, I would…
Passive when the action matters more than the person.
I see your point, but…
Tend to / might to avoid sounding absolute.
Although / even if… still… to concede, then keep your stance.
If I were / if I had for hypotheticals.
On the one hand… on the other… to show two sides.
Not really / not necessarily / perhaps to avoid sounding absolute.
I see your point, but… to disagree politely.
Instead of… I would… to offer another way.
It is not that… it is that… to reframe.
Spoken tone: skip furthermore / thus in a café talk.
contrasts: Although / still = concession. But is sharper.
If I were you = hypothetical, not a real plan.
Not really / not necessarily softens a claim.
I see your point, but… disagrees without a fight.
mistakes: Long sentences with no stance.
Disagreeing without an alternative.
Essay connectors (furthermore, thus) in a café conversation.
Using always / definitely with no evidence.
examples: Although I am tired, I still study for 15 minutes.
If I were late, I would send a message.
I understand you are busy, but I need this changed.
On the one hand it is convenient; on the other it is noisy.
This may not work for everyone.
Sorry, this dish is not right.
I have waited quite a long time.
Could you replace this for me?
I am a bit disappointed this time.
I would like to see the manager.
I hope next time it will be quicker.
If possible, I would like a partial refund.
I am still keeping a polite tone.
theory.applyPrompt: Give an opinion plus a contrast or condition.
theory.tip: B2 is tone control, not longer sentences for their own sake.
theory.structure: Sorry + the problem + ask to replace / refund. Stay polite.

theory.levelNote: Control stance: although, however, if I were, on the other hand. Soften disagreement.
points: Although / however for contrast.
Second conditional: If I were you, I would…
Passive when the action matters more than the person.
I see your point, but…
Tend to / might to avoid sounding absolute.
Although / even if… still… to concede, then keep your stance.
If I were / if I had for hypotheticals.
On the one hand… on the other… to show two sides.
Not really / not necessarily / perhaps to avoid sounding absolute.
I see your point, but… to disagree politely.
Instead of… I would… to offer another way.
It is not that… it is that… to reframe.
Spoken tone: skip furthermore / thus in a café talk.
contrasts: Although / still = concession. But is sharper.
If I were you = hypothetical, not a real plan.
Not really / not necessarily softens a claim.
I see your point, but… disagrees without a fight.
mistakes: Long sentences with no stance.
Disagreeing without an alternative.
Essay connectors (furthermore, thus) in a café conversation.
Using always / definitely with no evidence.

theory.levelNote: Control stance: although, however, if I were, on the other hand. Soften disagreement.
points: Although / however for contrast.
Second conditional: If I were you, I would…
Passive when the action matters more than the person.
I see your point, but…
Tend to / might to avoid sounding absolute.
Although / even if… still… to concede, then keep your stance.
If I were / if I had for hypotheticals.
On the one hand… on the other… to show two sides.
Not really / not necessarily / perhaps to avoid sounding absolute.
I see your point, but… to disagree politely.
Instead of… I would… to offer another way.
It is not that… it is that… to reframe.
Spoken tone: skip furthermore / thus in a café talk.
contrasts: Although / still = concession. But is sharper.
If I were you = hypothetical, not a real plan.
Not really / not necessarily softens a claim.
I see your point, but… disagrees without a fight.
mistakes: Long sentences with no stance.
Disagreeing without an alternative.
Essay connectors (furthermore, thus) in a café conversation.
Using always / definitely with no evidence.
examples: Although I am tired, I still study for 15 minutes.
If I were late, I would send a message.
I understand you are busy, but I need this changed.
On the one hand it is convenient; on the other it is noisy.
This may not work for everyone.
In my view, you should study more slowly.
If you are tired, then rest.
Don't cram too many words at once.
Avoid studying when you are angry.
It is better to speak in sentences.
theory.applyPrompt: Give an opinion plus a contrast or condition.
theory.tip: B2 is tone control, not longer sentences for their own sake.
theory.structure: Advice: should / shouldn't, try, if I were you; do not order.

theory.levelNote: Control stance: although, however, if I were, on the other hand. Soften disagreement.
points: Although / however for contrast.
Second conditional: If I were you, I would…
Passive when the action matters more than the person.
I see your point, but…
Tend to / might to avoid sounding absolute.
Although / even if… still… to concede, then keep your stance.
If I were / if I had for hypotheticals.
On the one hand… on the other… to show two sides.
Not really / not necessarily / perhaps to avoid sounding absolute.
I see your point, but… to disagree politely.
Instead of… I would… to offer another way.
It is not that… it is that… to reframe.
Spoken tone: skip furthermore / thus in a café talk.
contrasts: Although / still = concession. But is sharper.
If I were you = hypothetical, not a real plan.
Not really / not necessarily softens a claim.
I see your point, but… disagrees without a fight.
mistakes: Long sentences with no stance.
Disagreeing without an alternative.
Essay connectors (furthermore, thus) in a café conversation.
Using always / definitely with no evidence.
examples: Although I am tired, I still study for 15 minutes.
If I were late, I would send a message.
I understand you are busy, but I need this changed.
On the one hand it is convenient; on the other it is noisy.
This may not work for everyone.

theory.levelNote: Control stance: although, however, if I were, on the other hand. Soften disagreement.
points: Although / however for contrast.
Second conditional: If I were you, I would…
Passive when the action matters more than the person.
I see your point, but…
Tend to / might to avoid sounding absolute.
Although / even if… still… to concede, then keep your stance.
If I were / if I had for hypotheticals.
On the one hand… on the other… to show two sides.
Not really / not necessarily / perhaps to avoid sounding absolute.
I see your point, but… to disagree politely.
Instead of… I would… to offer another way.
It is not that… it is that… to reframe.
Spoken tone: skip furthermore / thus in a café talk.
contrasts: Although / still = concession. But is sharper.
If I were you = hypothetical, not a real plan.
Not really / not necessarily softens a claim.
I see your point, but… disagrees without a fight.
mistakes: Long sentences with no stance.
Disagreeing without an alternative.
Essay connectors (furthermore, thus) in a café conversation.
Using always / definitely with no evidence.
examples: Although I am tired, I still study for 15 minutes.
If I were late, I would send a message.
I understand you are busy, but I need this changed.
On the one hand it is convenient; on the other it is noisy.
This may not work for everyone.
I intend to go next month.
If it rains, I will reschedule.
It is not certain; it depends on work.
I am flexible about the time.
theory.applyPrompt: Give an opinion plus a contrast or condition.
theory.tip: B2 is tone control, not longer sentences for their own sake.
theory.structure: Intend / will / if… then reschedule. Say it is not certain when it is not fixed.

theory.levelNote: Control stance: although, however, if I were, on the other hand. Soften disagreement.
points: Although / however for contrast.
Second conditional: If I were you, I would…
Passive when the action matters more than the person.
I see your point, but…
Tend to / might to avoid sounding absolute.
Although / even if… still… to concede, then keep your stance.
If I were / if I had for hypotheticals.
On the one hand… on the other… to show two sides.
Not really / not necessarily / perhaps to avoid sounding absolute.
I see your point, but… to disagree politely.
Instead of… I would… to offer another way.
It is not that… it is that… to reframe.
Spoken tone: skip furthermore / thus in a café talk.
contrasts: Although / still = concession. But is sharper.
If I were you = hypothetical, not a real plan.
Not really / not necessarily softens a claim.
I see your point, but… disagrees without a fight.
mistakes: Long sentences with no stance.
Disagreeing without an alternative.
Essay connectors (furthermore, thus) in a café conversation.
Using always / definitely with no evidence.
examples: Although I am tired, I still study for 15 minutes.
If I were late, I would send a message.
I understand you are busy, but I need this changed.
On the one hand it is convenient; on the other it is noisy.
This may not work for everyone.
In the long run I want to be able to speak.
This week's priority is enough sleep.
Unless something urgent comes up, I will not cancel.
Later I will commit more clearly.

theory.tip: B2 is tone control, not longer sentences for their own sake.

theory.levelNote: Control stance: although, however, if I were, on the other hand. Soften disagreement.
points: Although / however for contrast.
Second conditional: If I were you, I would…
Passive when the action matters more than the person.
I see your point, but…
Tend to / might to avoid sounding absolute.
Although / even if… still… to concede, then keep your stance.
If I were / if I had for hypotheticals.
On the one hand… on the other… to show two sides.
Not really / not necessarily / perhaps to avoid sounding absolute.
I see your point, but… to disagree politely.
Instead of… I would… to offer another way.
It is not that… it is that… to reframe.
Spoken tone: skip furthermore / thus in a café talk.
contrasts: Although / still = concession. But is sharper.
If I were you = hypothetical, not a real plan.
Not really / not necessarily softens a claim.
I see your point, but… disagrees without a fight.
mistakes: Long sentences with no stance.
Disagreeing without an alternative.
Essay connectors (furthermore, thus) in a café conversation.
Using always / definitely with no evidence.
examples: Although I am tired, I still study for 15 minutes.
If I were late, I would send a message.
I understand you are busy, but I need this changed.
On the one hand it is convenient; on the other it is noisy.
This may not work for everyone.
Later I will commit more clearly.
Unless something urgent comes up, I will not cancel.
This week's priority is enough sleep.
In the long run I want to be able to speak.
For now, studying steadily is enough.
I am flexible about the time.
It is not certain; it depends on work.
If it rains, I will reschedule.
I intend to go next month.

theory.tip: B2 is tone control, not longer sentences for their own sake.
theory.structure: Intend / will / if… then reschedule. Say it is not certain when it is not fixed.

points: Although / however for contrast.
Second conditional: If I were you, I would…

contrasts: Although / still = concession. But is sharper.

theory.levelNote: Control stance: although, however, if I were, on the other hand. Soften disagreement.
points: Although / however for contrast.
Second conditional: If I were you, I would…
Passive when the action matters more than the person.
I see your point, but…
Tend to / might to avoid sounding absolute.
Although / even if… still… to concede, then keep your stance.
If I were / if I had for hypotheticals.
On the one hand… on the other… to show two sides.
Not really / not necessarily / perhaps to avoid sounding absolute.
I see your point, but… to disagree politely.
Instead of… I would… to offer another way.
It is not that… it is that… to reframe.
Spoken tone: skip furthermore / thus in a café talk.
contrasts: Although / still = concession. But is sharper.
If I were you = hypothetical, not a real plan.
Not really / not necessarily softens a claim.
I see your point, but… disagrees without a fight.
mistakes: Long sentences with no stance.
Disagreeing without an alternative.
Essay connectors (furthermore, thus) in a café conversation.
Using always / definitely with no evidence.
examples: Although I am tired, I still study for 15 minutes.
If I were late, I would send a message.
I understand you are busy, but I need this changed.
On the one hand it is convenient; on the other it is noisy.
This may not work for everyone.
I am sorry I spoke too fast.

theory.tip: B2 is tone control, not longer sentences for their own sake.

theory.levelNote: Control stance: although, however, if I were, on the other hand. Soften disagreement.
points: Although / however for contrast.
Second conditional: If I were you, I would…
Passive when the action matters more than the person.
I see your point, but…
Tend to / might to avoid sounding absolute.
Although / even if… still… to concede, then keep your stance.
If I were / if I had for hypotheticals.
On the one hand… on the other… to show two sides.
Not really / not necessarily / perhaps to avoid sounding absolute.
I see your point, but… to disagree politely.
Instead of… I would… to offer another way.
It is not that… it is that… to reframe.
Spoken tone: skip furthermore / thus in a café talk.
contrasts: Although / still = concession. But is sharper.
If I were you = hypothetical, not a real plan.
Not really / not necessarily softens a claim.
I see your point, but… disagrees without a fight.
mistakes: Long sentences with no stance.
Disagreeing without an alternative.
Essay connectors (furthermore, thus) in a café conversation.
Using always / definitely with no evidence.
examples: Although I am tired, I still study for 15 minutes.
If I were late, I would send a message.
I understand you are busy, but I need this changed.
On the one hand it is convenient; on the other it is noisy.
This may not work for everyone.
Keeping the peace makes it easier to breathe.
theory.applyPrompt: Give an opinion plus a contrast or condition.
theory.tip: B2 is tone control, not longer sentences for their own sake.
theory.structure: Relationships: I and…, we need to talk, sorry, a soft boundary.

theory.levelNote: Control stance: although, however, if I were, on the other hand. Soften disagreement.
points: Although / however for contrast.
Second conditional: If I were you, I would…
Passive when the action matters more than the person.
I see your point, but…
Tend to / might to avoid sounding absolute.
Although / even if… still… to concede, then keep your stance.
If I were / if I had for hypotheticals.
On the one hand… on the other… to show two sides.
Not really / not necessarily / perhaps to avoid sounding absolute.
I see your point, but… to disagree politely.
Instead of… I would… to offer another way.
It is not that… it is that… to reframe.
Spoken tone: skip furthermore / thus in a café talk.
contrasts: Although / still = concession. But is sharper.
If I were you = hypothetical, not a real plan.
Not really / not necessarily softens a claim.
I see your point, but… disagrees without a fight.
mistakes: Long sentences with no stance.
Disagreeing without an alternative.
Essay connectors (furthermore, thus) in a café conversation.
Using always / definitely with no evidence.
examples: Although I am tired, I still study for 15 minutes.
If I were late, I would send a message.
I understand you are busy, but I need this changed.
On the one hand it is convenient; on the other it is noisy.
This may not work for everyone.
I am sorry I spoke too fast.
It is not convenient to talk today.
Keeping the peace makes it easier to breathe.
theory.applyPrompt: Give an opinion plus a contrast or condition.
theory.tip: B2 is tone control, not longer sentences for their own sake.
theory.structure: Relationships: I and…, we need to talk, sorry, a soft boundary.

theory.levelNote: Control stance: although, however, if I were, on the other hand. Soften disagreement.
points: Although / however for contrast.
Second conditional: If I were you, I would…
Passive when the action matters more than the person.
I see your point, but…
Tend to / might to avoid sounding absolute.
Although / even if… still… to concede, then keep your stance.
If I were / if I had for hypotheticals.
On the one hand… on the other… to show two sides.
Not really / not necessarily / perhaps to avoid sounding absolute.
I see your point, but… to disagree politely.
Instead of… I would… to offer another way.
It is not that… it is that… to reframe.
Spoken tone: skip furthermore / thus in a café talk.
contrasts: Although / still = concession. But is sharper.
If I were you = hypothetical, not a real plan.
Not really / not necessarily softens a claim.
I see your point, but… disagrees without a fight.
mistakes: Long sentences with no stance.
Disagreeing without an alternative.
Essay connectors (furthermore, thus) in a café conversation.
Using always / definitely with no evidence.
examples: Although I am tired, I still study for 15 minutes.
If I were late, I would send a message.
I understand you are busy, but I need this changed.
On the one hand it is convenient; on the other it is noisy.
This may not work for everyone.
I am sorry I spoke too fast.
Don't push me to answer at once.
theory.applyPrompt: Give an opinion plus a contrast or condition.
theory.tip: B2 is tone control, not longer sentences for their own sake.

points: Although / however for contrast.
Second conditional: If I were you, I would…
Passive when the action matters more than the person.

Although / even if… still… to concede, then keep your stance.

Not really / not necessarily / perhaps to avoid sounding absolute.

Instead of… I would… to offer another way.
It is not that… it is that… to reframe.
Spoken tone: skip furthermore / thus in a café talk.
contrasts: Although / still = concession. But is sharper.
If I were you = hypothetical, not a real plan.
Not really / not necessarily softens a claim.
I see your point, but… disagrees without a fight.
mistakes: Long sentences with no stance.
Disagreeing without an alternative.
Essay connectors (furthermore, thus) in a café conversation.
Using always / definitely with no evidence.

points: Past simple: I went, she had, we did.

Going to + verb for a near plan.
Comparative: adjective + -er, or more + adjective.
Could you…? / Can I…? for polite requests.
Why? to ask for a short reason.
Before / after + time or clause.
Too / enough: too spicy, not big enough.
contrasts: I am eating (now) vs I ate (finished) vs I am going to eat (plan).

Could I…? is softer than Can I…?

theory.levelNote: Control stance: although, however, if I were, on the other hand. Soften disagreement.
points: Although / however for contrast.
Second conditional: If I were you, I would…
Passive when the action matters more than the person.
I see your point, but…
Tend to / might to avoid sounding absolute.
Although / even if… still… to concede, then keep your stance.
If I were / if I had for hypotheticals.
On the one hand… on the other… to show two sides.
Not really / not necessarily / perhaps to avoid sounding absolute.
I see your point, but… to disagree politely.
Instead of… I would… to offer another way.
It is not that… it is that… to reframe.
Spoken tone: skip furthermore / thus in a café talk.
contrasts: Although / still = concession. But is sharper.
If I were you = hypothetical, not a real plan.
Not really / not necessarily softens a claim.
I see your point, but… disagrees without a fight.
mistakes: Long sentences with no stance.
Disagreeing without an alternative.
Essay connectors (furthermore, thus) in a café conversation.
Using always / definitely with no evidence.
examples: Although I am tired, I still study for 15 minutes.
If I were late, I would send a message.
I understand you are busy, but I need this changed.
On the one hand it is convenient; on the other it is noisy.
This may not work for everyone.
I think 15 minutes a day is better than one long session.
I agree, because the mind needs time to file things away.
For example, learn words by real situations.
However, some people still need a longer class.
Overall, a steady rhythm matters more than the minutes.
On the one hand, exams give a target.
On the other hand, exams can make people rush.
There is evidence from daily habits.
Conclusion: go slowly and keep it.
We should state the reason clearly.

theory.tip: B2 is tone control, not longer sentences for their own sake.

theory.levelNote: Control stance: although, however, if I were, on the other hand. Soften disagreement.
points: Although / however for contrast.
Second conditional: If I were you, I would…
Passive when the action matters more than the person.
I see your point, but…
Tend to / might to avoid sounding absolute.
Although / even if… still… to concede, then keep your stance.
If I were / if I had for hypotheticals.
On the one hand… on the other… to show two sides.
Not really / not necessarily / perhaps to avoid sounding absolute.
I see your point, but… to disagree politely.
Instead of… I would… to offer another way.
It is not that… it is that… to reframe.
Spoken tone: skip furthermore / thus in a café talk.
contrasts: Although / still = concession. But is sharper.
If I were you = hypothetical, not a real plan.
Not really / not necessarily softens a claim.
I see your point, but… disagrees without a fight.
mistakes: Long sentences with no stance.
Disagreeing without an alternative.
Essay connectors (furthermore, thus) in a café conversation.
Using always / definitely with no evidence.
examples: Although I am tired, I still study for 15 minutes.
If I were late, I would send a message.
I understand you are busy, but I need this changed.
On the one hand it is convenient; on the other it is noisy.
This may not work for everyone.
I think 15 minutes a day is better than one long session.
I agree, because the mind needs time to file things away.
For example, learn words by real situations.
theory.applyPrompt: Give an opinion plus a contrast or condition.
theory.tip: B2 is tone control, not longer sentences for their own sake.
theory.structure: Opinion: I think, not really, a short reason, ask what they think.

theory.levelNote: Control stance: although, however, if I were, on the other hand. Soften disagreement.
points: Although / however for contrast.
Second conditional: If I were you, I would…
Passive when the action matters more than the person.
I see your point, but…
Tend to / might to avoid sounding absolute.
Although / even if… still… to concede, then keep your stance.
If I were / if I had for hypotheticals.
On the one hand… on the other… to show two sides.
Not really / not necessarily / perhaps to avoid sounding absolute.
I see your point, but… to disagree politely.
Instead of… I would… to offer another way.
It is not that… it is that… to reframe.
Spoken tone: skip furthermore / thus in a café talk.
contrasts: Although / still = concession. But is sharper.
If I were you = hypothetical, not a real plan.
Not really / not necessarily softens a claim.
I see your point, but… disagrees without a fight.
mistakes: Long sentences with no stance.
Disagreeing without an alternative.
Essay connectors (furthermore, thus) in a café conversation.
Using always / definitely with no evidence.
examples: Although I am tired, I still study for 15 minutes.
If I were late, I would send a message.
I understand you are busy, but I need this changed.
On the one hand it is convenient; on the other it is noisy.
This may not work for everyone.
I think 15 minutes a day is better than one long session.
I agree, because the mind needs time to file things away.
For example, learn words by real situations.
However, some people still need a longer class.
Overall, a steady rhythm matters more than the minutes.
On the one hand, exams give a target.
On the other hand, exams can make people rush.
There is evidence from daily habits.

We should state the reason clearly.

theory.levelNote: Control stance: although, however, if I were, on the other hand. Soften disagreement.
points: Although / however for contrast.
Second conditional: If I were you, I would…
Passive when the action matters more than the person.
I see your point, but…
Tend to / might to avoid sounding absolute.
Although / even if… still… to concede, then keep your stance.
If I were / if I had for hypotheticals.
On the one hand… on the other… to show two sides.
Not really / not necessarily / perhaps to avoid sounding absolute.
I see your point, but… to disagree politely.
Instead of… I would… to offer another way.
It is not that… it is that… to reframe.
Spoken tone: skip furthermore / thus in a café talk.
contrasts: Although / still = concession. But is sharper.
If I were you = hypothetical, not a real plan.
Not really / not necessarily softens a claim.
I see your point, but… disagrees without a fight.
mistakes: Long sentences with no stance.
Disagreeing without an alternative.
Essay connectors (furthermore, thus) in a café conversation.
Using always / definitely with no evidence.

theory.levelNote: Control stance: although, however, if I were, on the other hand. Soften disagreement.
points: Although / however for contrast.
Second conditional: If I were you, I would…
Passive when the action matters more than the person.
I see your point, but…
Tend to / might to avoid sounding absolute.
Although / even if… still… to concede, then keep your stance.
If I were / if I had for hypotheticals.
On the one hand… on the other… to show two sides.
Not really / not necessarily / perhaps to avoid sounding absolute.
I see your point, but… to disagree politely.
Instead of… I would… to offer another way.
It is not that… it is that… to reframe.
Spoken tone: skip furthermore / thus in a café talk.
contrasts: Although / still = concession. But is sharper.
If I were you = hypothetical, not a real plan.
Not really / not necessarily softens a claim.
I see your point, but… disagrees without a fight.
mistakes: Long sentences with no stance.
Disagreeing without an alternative.
Essay connectors (furthermore, thus) in a café conversation.
Using always / definitely with no evidence.
examples: Although I am tired, I still study for 15 minutes.
If I were late, I would send a message.
I understand you are busy, but I need this changed.
On the one hand it is convenient; on the other it is noisy.
This may not work for everyone.
I think 15 minutes a day is better than one long session.
I agree, because the mind needs time to file things away.
For example, learn words by real situations.
However, some people still need a longer class.
Overall, a steady rhythm matters more than the minutes.
theory.applyPrompt: Give an opinion plus a contrast or condition.
theory.tip: B2 is tone control, not longer sentences for their own sake.

theory.levelNote: Control stance: although, however, if I were, on the other hand. Soften disagreement.
points: Although / however for contrast.
Second conditional: If I were you, I would…
Passive when the action matters more than the person.
I see your point, but…
Tend to / might to avoid sounding absolute.
Although / even if… still… to concede, then keep your stance.
If I were / if I had for hypotheticals.
On the one hand… on the other… to show two sides.
Not really / not necessarily / perhaps to avoid sounding absolute.
I see your point, but… to disagree politely.
Instead of… I would… to offer another way.
It is not that… it is that… to reframe.
Spoken tone: skip furthermore / thus in a café talk.
contrasts: Although / still = concession. But is sharper.
If I were you = hypothetical, not a real plan.
Not really / not necessarily softens a claim.
I see your point, but… disagrees without a fight.
mistakes: Long sentences with no stance.
Disagreeing without an alternative.
Essay connectors (furthermore, thus) in a café conversation.
Using always / definitely with no evidence.
examples: Although I am tired, I still study for 15 minutes.
If I were late, I would send a message.
I understand you are busy, but I need this changed.
On the one hand it is convenient; on the other it is noisy.
This may not work for everyone.
I need support with this report.
Could you send me an update?
The project is a bit overdue.
I will send a short email.
theory.applyPrompt: Give an opinion plus a contrast or condition.
theory.tip: B2 is tone control, not longer sentences for their own sake.
theory.structure: Work: what I do, a meeting, a deadline, time off, ask for support.

theory.levelNote: Control stance: although, however, if I were, on the other hand. Soften disagreement.
points: Although / however for contrast.
Second conditional: If I were you, I would…
Passive when the action matters more than the person.
I see your point, but…
Tend to / might to avoid sounding absolute.
Although / even if… still… to concede, then keep your stance.
If I were / if I had for hypotheticals.
On the one hand… on the other… to show two sides.
Not really / not necessarily / perhaps to avoid sounding absolute.
I see your point, but… to disagree politely.
Instead of… I would… to offer another way.
It is not that… it is that… to reframe.
Spoken tone: skip furthermore / thus in a café talk.
contrasts: Although / still = concession. But is sharper.
If I were you = hypothetical, not a real plan.
Not really / not necessarily softens a claim.
I see your point, but… disagrees without a fight.
mistakes: Long sentences with no stance.
Disagreeing without an alternative.
Essay connectors (furthermore, thus) in a café conversation.
Using always / definitely with no evidence.
examples: Although I am tired, I still study for 15 minutes.
If I were late, I would send a message.
I understand you are busy, but I need this changed.
On the one hand it is convenient; on the other it is noisy.
This may not work for everyone.
Each person is responsible for a part.
theory.applyPrompt: Give an opinion plus a contrast or condition.
theory.tip: B2 is tone control, not longer sentences for their own sake.

theory.levelNote: Control stance: although, however, if I were, on the other hand. Soften disagreement.
points: Although / however for contrast.
Second conditional: If I were you, I would…
Passive when the action matters more than the person.
I see your point, but…
Tend to / might to avoid sounding absolute.
Although / even if… still… to concede, then keep your stance.
If I were / if I had for hypotheticals.
On the one hand… on the other… to show two sides.
Not really / not necessarily / perhaps to avoid sounding absolute.
I see your point, but… to disagree politely.
Instead of… I would… to offer another way.
It is not that… it is that… to reframe.
Spoken tone: skip furthermore / thus in a café talk.
contrasts: Although / still = concession. But is sharper.
If I were you = hypothetical, not a real plan.
Not really / not necessarily softens a claim.
I see your point, but… disagrees without a fight.
mistakes: Long sentences with no stance.
Disagreeing without an alternative.
Essay connectors (furthermore, thus) in a café conversation.
Using always / definitely with no evidence.
examples: Although I am tired, I still study for 15 minutes.
If I were late, I would send a message.
I understand you are busy, but I need this changed.
On the one hand it is convenient; on the other it is noisy.
This may not work for everyone.
The air in the city is poor today.
Cycling is good for health and the environment.
The community can plant more trees.
The future depends on what we do today.
Each person is responsible for a part.

theory.levelNote: Control stance: although, however, if I were, on the other hand. Soften disagreement.
points: Although / however for contrast.
Second conditional: If I were you, I would…
Passive when the action matters more than the person.
I see your point, but…
Tend to / might to avoid sounding absolute.
Although / even if… still… to concede, then keep your stance.
If I were / if I had for hypotheticals.
On the one hand… on the other… to show two sides.
Not really / not necessarily / perhaps to avoid sounding absolute.
I see your point, but… to disagree politely.
Instead of… I would… to offer another way.
It is not that… it is that… to reframe.
Spoken tone: skip furthermore / thus in a café talk.
contrasts: Although / still = concession. But is sharper.
If I were you = hypothetical, not a real plan.
Not really / not necessarily softens a claim.
I see your point, but… disagrees without a fight.
mistakes: Long sentences with no stance.
Disagreeing without an alternative.
Essay connectors (furthermore, thus) in a café conversation.
Using always / definitely with no evidence.
examples: Although I am tired, I still study for 15 minutes.
If I were late, I would send a message.
I understand you are busy, but I need this changed.
On the one hand it is convenient; on the other it is noisy.
This may not work for everyone.
Fifteen minutes of self-study still counts.
Exams create pressure, but they are not everything.
Memory needs a steady rhythm, not stuffing.

theory.levelNote: Control stance: although, however, if I were, on the other hand. Soften disagreement.
points: Although / however for contrast.
Second conditional: If I were you, I would…
Passive when the action matters more than the person.
I see your point, but…
Tend to / might to avoid sounding absolute.
Although / even if… still… to concede, then keep your stance.
If I were / if I had for hypotheticals.
On the one hand… on the other… to show two sides.
Not really / not necessarily / perhaps to avoid sounding absolute.
I see your point, but… to disagree politely.
Instead of… I would… to offer another way.
It is not that… it is that… to reframe.
Spoken tone: skip furthermore / thus in a café talk.
contrasts: Although / still = concession. But is sharper.
If I were you = hypothetical, not a real plan.
Not really / not necessarily softens a claim.
I see your point, but… disagrees without a fight.
mistakes: Long sentences with no stance.
Disagreeing without an alternative.
Essay connectors (furthermore, thus) in a café conversation.
Using always / definitely with no evidence.
examples: Although I am tired, I still study for 15 minutes.
If I were late, I would send a message.
I understand you are busy, but I need this changed.
On the one hand it is convenient; on the other it is noisy.
This may not work for everyone.
A good teacher keeps lessons small and clear.
Results come slowly, and that is normal.
I feel anxious before I speak.
Confidence comes after a few correct lines.
Good materials do not replace the habit.
This week's goal: four small sessions.

theory.levelNote: Control stance: although, however, if I were, on the other hand. Soften disagreement.
points: Although / however for contrast.
Second conditional: If I were you, I would…
Passive when the action matters more than the person.
I see your point, but…
Tend to / might to avoid sounding absolute.
Although / even if… still… to concede, then keep your stance.
If I were / if I had for hypotheticals.
On the one hand… on the other… to show two sides.
Not really / not necessarily / perhaps to avoid sounding absolute.
I see your point, but… to disagree politely.
Instead of… I would… to offer another way.
It is not that… it is that… to reframe.
Spoken tone: skip furthermore / thus in a café talk.
contrasts: Although / still = concession. But is sharper.
If I were you = hypothetical, not a real plan.
Not really / not necessarily softens a claim.
I see your point, but… disagrees without a fight.
mistakes: Long sentences with no stance.
Disagreeing without an alternative.
Essay connectors (furthermore, thus) in a café conversation.
Using always / definitely with no evidence.

This may not work for everyone.

theory.levelNote: Control stance: although, however, if I were, on the other hand. Soften disagreement.
points: Although / however for contrast.
Second conditional: If I were you, I would…
Passive when the action matters more than the person.
I see your point, but…
Tend to / might to avoid sounding absolute.
Although / even if… still… to concede, then keep your stance.
If I were / if I had for hypotheticals.
On the one hand… on the other… to show two sides.
Not really / not necessarily / perhaps to avoid sounding absolute.
I see your point, but… to disagree politely.
Instead of… I would… to offer another way.
It is not that… it is that… to reframe.
Spoken tone: skip furthermore / thus in a café talk.
contrasts: Although / still = concession. But is sharper.
If I were you = hypothetical, not a real plan.
Not really / not necessarily softens a claim.
I see your point, but… disagrees without a fight.
mistakes: Long sentences with no stance.
Disagreeing without an alternative.
Essay connectors (furthermore, thus) in a café conversation.
Using always / definitely with no evidence.
examples: Although I am tired, I still study for 15 minutes.
If I were late, I would send a message.
I understand you are busy, but I need this changed.
On the one hand it is convenient; on the other it is noisy.
This may not work for everyone.

theory.levelNote: Control stance: although, however, if I were, on the other hand. Soften disagreement.
points: Although / however for contrast.
Second conditional: If I were you, I would…
Passive when the action matters more than the person.
I see your point, but…
Tend to / might to avoid sounding absolute.
Although / even if… still… to concede, then keep your stance.
If I were / if I had for hypotheticals.
On the one hand… on the other… to show two sides.
Not really / not necessarily / perhaps to avoid sounding absolute.
I see your point, but… to disagree politely.
Instead of… I would… to offer another way.
It is not that… it is that… to reframe.
Spoken tone: skip furthermore / thus in a café talk.
contrasts: Although / still = concession. But is sharper.
If I were you = hypothetical, not a real plan.
Not really / not necessarily softens a claim.
I see your point, but… disagrees without a fight.
mistakes: Long sentences with no stance.
Disagreeing without an alternative.
Essay connectors (furthermore, thus) in a café conversation.
Using always / definitely with no evidence.
examples: Although I am tired, I still study for 15 minutes.
If I were late, I would send a message.
I understand you are busy, but I need this changed.
On the one hand it is convenient; on the other it is noisy.
This may not work for everyone.

theory.levelNote: Control stance: although, however, if I were, on the other hand. Soften disagreement.
points: Although / however for contrast.
Second conditional: If I were you, I would…
Passive when the action matters more than the person.
I see your point, but…
Tend to / might to avoid sounding absolute.
Although / even if… still… to concede, then keep your stance.
If I were / if I had for hypotheticals.
On the one hand… on the other… to show two sides.
Not really / not necessarily / perhaps to avoid sounding absolute.
I see your point, but… to disagree politely.
Instead of… I would… to offer another way.
It is not that… it is that… to reframe.
Spoken tone: skip furthermore / thus in a café talk.
contrasts: Although / still = concession. But is sharper.
If I were you = hypothetical, not a real plan.
Not really / not necessarily softens a claim.
I see your point, but… disagrees without a fight.
mistakes: Long sentences with no stance.
Disagreeing without an alternative.
Essay connectors (furthermore, thus) in a café conversation.
Using always / definitely with no evidence.
examples: Although I am tired, I still study for 15 minutes.
If I were late, I would send a message.
I understand you are busy, but I need this changed.
On the one hand it is convenient; on the other it is noisy.
This may not work for everyone.
Fifteen minutes of self-study still counts.
Exams create pressure, but they are not everything.
Memory needs a steady rhythm, not stuffing.
Failing one lesson is not failing the path.
Motivation comes from a sentence you can say.
Students need a balance of rest and practice.

theory.tip: B2 is tone control, not longer sentences for their own sake.
